one_liner: Computational pathology group building tile-level foundation models for colorectal cancer.
summary: We pretrain vision transformers on whole-slide images and fine-tune for prognostic stratification. We have published on weakly supervised survival prediction from H&E slides. We need a large, outcome-linked histopathology archive. Our pipeline assumes local GPU training on data staged to our own cluster.
_test_case: Should rank RPAZ Zuid at or near 100. Should be HARD BLOCKED against UKN Nordharz and CHR Garonne despite good domain fit, because it requires export and has neither TRE nor federated capability. This pair is the single most important assertion in the test suite.

one_liner: Federated learning group specialising in longitudinal neuroimaging under strict data residency.
summary: Nous développons des modèles de progression lésionnelle entraînés en fédéré, sans mouvement de données. Notre stack est déployée sur cinq sites hospitaliers. Nous cherchons des partenaires disposant de cohortes IRM longitudinales qui ne peuvent pas exporter leurs données.
_test_case: The governance-capable team. Should score near-perfect against CHR Garonne AND score respectably against UKN Nordharz despite the domain mismatch, because access-model compatibility carries 18 points. If this team does not outrank Elbe Vision Lab on total portfolio of viable matches, the access_model weight is set too low.

one_liner: Causal inference on population-scale prescribing data for drug repurposing signals.
summary: We run target trial emulation and high-dimensional confounding adjustment on national claims and prescribing registries. Our analysts routinely work inside third-party trusted research environments and we have completed nine TRE onboardings across four countries.
_test_case: Tests that the United Kingdom is treated as ELIGIBLE. Most people assume post-Brexit exclusion; SPRIND's rules explicitly include the UK. If your country list gets this wrong you will silently hide a large share of Europe's best epidemiology teams. Should match Aurora Registry Node strongly.

org_name: Aleph Genomics Group, Negev Institute for Computational Biology
one_liner: Knowledge-graph and sequence models for variant prioritisation in undiagnosed disease.
summary: We combine phenotype ontology embeddings with variant effect prediction to shortlist causal variants in undiagnosed patients. Our methods are validated on published trio cohorts and we are seeking a new, unpublished cohort for prospective evaluation.
_test_case: Two tests. (1) Israel is ELIGIBLE under SPRIND's rules — verify the country list. (2) Perfect domain match with ISEA Alpenraum (rare disease, paediatrics, genomics, exportable) but ISEA has under 1,000 subjects against a stated need of 10k–100k. This must produce a HIGH score with a VISIBLE scale warning, not a low score. Getting this wrong in either direction means the graded scale penalty is mistuned. Note also: this team's Hebrew requires adding 'he' to the languages enum.

one_liner: Digital pathology foundation models; US-headquartered, seeking European collaboration.
summary: We are headquartered in Boston and understand we cannot lead an application. We are listing as a potential collaboration partner for a European-led team and can contribute pretrained pathology encoders and annotation capacity.
_test_case: SCHEMA GAP, deliberately included. On every substantive field this is the best possible partner for RPAZ Zuid — but eligible_hq is false, so the current rules hard-block it to zero. That is wrong: SPRIND's rules allow individual team members and collaboration partners to sit outside the EU/EFTA/UK/IL region; only the APPLICANT HQ must be inside it. The schema needs a boolean 'partner_only' distinct from 'eligible_hq', and the scorer needs a rule: partner_only profiles are excluded from ranking as a lead applicant but remain visible and matchable as collaborators. Fix this before building the scorer.
